findings.location: <article> introductory parenthetical reference after opening italic line
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the book name into Portuguese using conventional forms. Replace “(John 10:22)” with “(João 10:22)” and preserve the chapter:verse format and parentheses.

Translate each English book name to its conventional Portuguese form while keeping chapter and verse numbers unchanged. Suggested replacements: “(John 10:20)” → “(João 10:20)”; “(John 1:46)” → “(João 1:46)”; “(1 Kings 1:6)” → “(1 Reis 1:6)”; “(Genesis 25:8)” → “(Gênesis 25:8)”; “(Acts 5:12)” → “(Atos 5:12)”; “(Matthew 24:12)” → “(Mateus 24:12)”.

findings.source_quote: Little praise arises for the season that greets him at his weakest point and seeks to discomfort and discourage him from the zest of life.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct typographical error and ensure natural Portuguese: change “Pouenos elogios surgem” to “Poucos elogios surgem” (or an equally natural rendering).
findings.translation_quote: Pouenos elogios surgem para a estação que o encontra em seu ponto mais fraco e procura desconfortá‑lo e desanimá‑lo da alegria de viver.

findings.location: Heading for the final thematic section (source: "Sympathy")
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the section heading to a proper Portuguese equivalent. Replace the mistranslated/misspelled header “Simpadeia” with a suitable rendering such as “Compaixão” or “Simpatia” (preferably “Compaixão” to match the nuance of the original).

Use the conventional Portuguese abbreviation/form for Ecclesiastes. Replace “(Ecc. 4:11)” with “(Ecl. 4:11)” or “(Eccl.)” only if the publication’s house style prefers that—ensure book name matches other converted forms (for example “(Ecl. 4:11)”).

findings.location: Choice of some vocabulary / register (first paragraph: “humidade”)
findings.suggested_fix: For broader international Portuguese clarity prefer “umidade” over European “humidade”. Change “humidade” to “umidade” unless the magazine targets European Portuguese specifically.
